correctness.rationale: Huang–Jenkinson–Xu–Zhang Theorem D supplies exact f-mu(f)=c_f(Phi-alpha)+u∘sigma-u, |c_f|≤Lip/(1-theta)^2 and |u|Lip≤theta Lip/(1-theta)^3. Sturmian digit balance gives |S_n(Phi-alpha)|<1. Summation and diameter≤1 give the claimed [n(1-theta)^3]^-1 Wasserstein estimate by duality; triangle inequality and Birkhoff–von Neumann equal-weights transport give the upper F_n bound. For every irrational n alpha, the two possible digit counts floor(n alpha),ceil(n alpha) both occur, and the first-symbol 1-Lipschitz observable proves sup F_n≥1/n. Every n and every irrational alpha is covered without finite approximation; constants are upper bounds, not claimed optimum.

originality.rationale: This claimed endpoint Wasserstein and matching theorem is a near-immediate corollary of published Huang–Jenkinson–Xu–Zhang Theorem D (arXiv:2610.03619v1, October 2 2026) and its own explicit Sturmian balance lemma, combined only with standard Wasserstein duality and the permutation representation. The source contains precisely the quantitative Lipschitz constants and uniform balance needed; the lower bound follows mechanically from two adjacent word counts. Under claim-versus-prior implication and corollary coverage rules, a previously proved stronger cohomological statement covers the substance even though it does not spell out the n^-1 matching theorem.
